title: The Hidden Risk Inside Your Most Important Workflows: New Study Exposes Security Weak Points
summary: Did you know 64% of organizations experience mission-critical failures? Review a recent study on security gaps in mission-critical collaboration today!
body_markdown:
PALO ALTO, Calif., July 30, 2025 /PRNewswire/ — Mattermost, the secure collaboration platform for mission-critical work, today announced the release of “Optimizing What Matters Most: The State of Mission-Critical Work,” a comprehensive research study conducted independently by the Ponemon Institute. The study reveals alarming vulnerabilities in how organizations protect their most critical operations, with 64% of organizations experiencing an average of six mission-critical workflow disruptions or failures in the past year.


The research exposes a dangerous disconnect between the importance of mission-critical workflows — the tasks, systems or processes within an organization that are essential for its operations and survival — and how well they’re protected. Only 47% of respondents understand the risk profile of their mission-critical workflows, while just 52% feel confident in their privacy and security measures.


The study also found dedicated teams drive better outcomes; organizations with dedicated mission-critical workflow teams report 10% fewer disruptions and are nearly twice the process efficiency (57% vs 36%). These “high performers” are also more likely to adopt purpose-built mission-critical collaboration tools and measure the costs of disruptions to improve future execution.


The Security Gap in Mission-Critical Collaboration


Despite working in the highly sensitive sectors of defense, government, and critical infrastructure, most organizations lack effective protection for the very workflows that keep their operations running.


Workflow Failures Are the New Normal


Cyberattacks are now the leading cause of critical workflow disruptions, cited by 50% of respondents. The fallout is severe:


“This research confirms a silent crisis: too many mission-critical operations are run on legacy collaboration platforms, technology that was never intended for high-stakes, secure environments,” said Ian Tien, CEO of Mattermost. “While 61% of organizations recognize a strong security posture is critical, too many are still relying on general enterprise tools that leave them vulnerable when the mission is on the line.”


AI Adoption Brings Both Promise and Peril


With 51% of organizations adopting AI to automate critical tasks, 53% of adopters already report data leakage or theft as a major concern.

About Ponemon Institute


Ponemon Institute is dedicated to independent research and education that advances responsible information and privacy management practices within business and government. The Institute conducts high quality, empirical studies on critical issues affecting the management and security of sensitive information about people and organizations.
